summary.text: Wife of Idomeneus king of Crete, who took Leucus as lover when Nauplius corrupted the Greek wives — and was killed with her daughter Clisithyra before the victor of Troy could land.

story.text: Apollodorus names Meda among the wives Nauplius turned false while coasting along Hellas: Clytemnestra with Aegisthus, Aegialia with Cometes, and Meda with Leucus. The nested episode on Nauplius' vengeance tells the contrivance; the nested episode on Idomeneus and Leucus tells the Cretan end.
Leucus killed Meda and her daughter Clisithyra, who had taken refuge in the temple, before Idomeneus returned from Troy — murder in sanctuary that completed the coup over ten Cretan cities.
